I don't know if I'm the only one, but the picture looks really fake to me.

What are the contents of the other writings? What is the SCP writing essays about?

Why have we not searched the insides of this tower? I don't really feel the Foundation wanting to stay away from "a stalker girlfriend" is satisfying enough of a reason to have no Exploration Log. Send a robot in.

What happens if a human is seen by the servitors? Do they go crazy? Do they act extremely shy like a stereotypical school girl in love? Wouldn't there be records of human interaction from when the Foundation discovered the thing?

I feel there's so much potential in this SCP, considering what's already there, for it to stop short like it does

item.title: Thank you!
item.content:encoded: For a little while now, I've been reading a few of the articles on this site. A few were bad, and a lot were good. Really good. But I have to say that this was definitely the article that sealed the deal for me. I just had to register to the site simply to leave a comment and thank you for this. item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I refer you to Moose's post on the matter, in response to a similar post:

What? Oh god, no. This thing is fucking crazy. The best containment procedures involve staying as far away from it as fucking possible, like a teenage girl keeping her distance from the crazy drunk homeless guy in the alley who JUST WANTS TO BE FRIENDS WITH THE PRETTY LADY.

Yes, I know the Foundation aren't teenage girls (mostly), but think about it. What happens if this thing gets too much exposure to humans and decides that we're not the Great Ones it was looking for after all?

The Foundation has a pretty good idea of this thing's strengths, and know that this thing is potentially very dangerous if it changes its mind. It might be in-character for the Foundation to try to explore this thing, but it would be a very bad idea, and they're probably smart enough to know it.
